description: A claim contradicted by a credible denial, an official correction or a retraction. The design's answer is CONFLICTED or REJECTED, both NO_EFFECT. When the claim and the denial come from different domains the rules see two families, so the classifier must notice that they disagree.

cases.summary: A rumored hack, then the exchange denies it through a credible outlet.

items.title: Exchange Meridex hacked again, insiders say
Meridex denies new hack reports, says all wallets secure and withdrawals normal

cases.why: One rumor source and a credible denial: conflicted.

cases.summary: An emergency-hike rumor, then officials deny it.

items.title: Fed preparing surprise emergency hike, sources claim
Fed officials deny any plan for an emergency rate move

cases.why: The only report of the claim is contradicted by a credible denial.

cases.summary: A reported tanker attack, then the navy says it was an engine fire.

items.title: Tanker attacked near Strait of Hormuz, reports say
Navy says no attack occurred; tanker reported an engine-room fire

cases.why: An official account contradicts the attack report.

cases.summary: A site reports an approval, then retracts it.

items.title: SEC approves spot ether ETF staking for all issuers
Correction: SEC has not approved ETF staking; earlier report was in error

cases.why: The publisher retracted its own report; it was also bullish and single-source.

cases.summary: A breach rumor, contradicted by the exchange's own status page.

items.title: Coinbase suffers massive breach, users report empty accounts
Resolved: some users saw incorrect balances in the app
items.excerpt: A display issue caused some users to see incorrect balances in the mobile app. Balances were never affected and the issue is resolved.

cases.why: The official source explains the reports as a display bug: the breach claim is contradicted.
